title: Instruction-Level Abstraction (ILA): A Uniform Specification for System-on-Chip (SoC) Verification
reading_scope: Primary full text inspected; introduction, formal model, modeling/verification case studies, discussion, related work, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Accelerator-rich SoCs lack a uniform formal software-visible hardware specification.
general_principle: Model processors and accelerators uniformly as hierarchical instruction-level state-transition abstractions.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Equivalence checking between ILAs and between an ILA and an FSM implementation under a formal execution semantics.
practical_connection: AES, Gaussian-blur, RBM accelerators and a RISC-V processor; modeling and verification case studies.
evaluation_breadth: Several accelerator domains plus one general-purpose processor.
artifact_strength: Formal definitions and detailed case studies; tool-backed verification context, but not a delivered dependency-cut certificate.
narrative_sequence: Heterogeneous-SoC specification gap -> ILA semantics and hierarchy -> modeling/verification case studies -> boundary and future uses.
delta_for_this_project: Provides a richer functional interface abstraction; it does not certify a supplied bounded dependency cut, final-context minimality, or canonical first-completion diagnostics.

title: Application-Level Validation of Accelerator Designs Using a Formal Software/Hardware Interface
reading_scope: Primary full text inspected; motivation, interface formalization, validation workflow, case studies, evaluation, limitations, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Application-level accelerator validation is expensive and software/hardware interfaces are frequently underspecified.
general_principle: Use an ILA-based formal interface to connect application software behavior with accelerator implementations and flexible matching.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Compositional refinement/equivalence obligations and solver-aided matching validate software-visible behavior across abstraction levels.
practical_connection: End-to-end accelerator application case studies, including detection of a concrete design flaw.
evaluation_breadth: Multiple accelerator/application stacks with software and hardware components.
artifact_strength: Systematic formal workflow and case studies; focuses on application-level functional validation rather than timing-slice certificates.
narrative_sequence: Application validation gap -> formal interface -> matching/refinement workflow -> case studies and discovered defect -> limitations.
delta_for_this_project: Validates a richer application interface; the present work instead gives a small consumer-side certificate for one bounded first-completion cut.

title: LightningSim: Fast and Accurate Trace-Based Simulation for High-Level Synthesis
reading_scope: Primary full text inspected; architecture, trace/schedule method, stall/deadlock handling, evaluation, related work, and limitations calibrated.
motivating_problem: C simulation misses hardware timing while RTL co-simulation is too slow for iterative HLS development.
general_principle: Combine an LLVM execution trace with static HLS scheduling information to reconstruct cycle behavior quickly.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Timing is checked empirically against HLS RTL co-simulation; the model also analyzes stalls and deadlocks.
practical_connection: A tool integrated with HLS workflows for rapid design iteration.
evaluation_breadth: Thirty-three reported benchmarks with timing-accuracy and speed comparisons.
artifact_strength: Executable simulator and comparative evaluation; no independent proof object for each discarded dependency.
narrative_sequence: Slow RTL feedback -> trace/schedule reconstruction -> implementation -> accuracy/speed/deadlock evaluation -> scope limits.
delta_for_this_project: Optimizes simulation accuracy and speed; this project measures checker evidence for a supplied bounded cut and makes no throughput claim.

title: OmniSim: Simulating Hardware with C Speed and RTL Accuracy for High-Level Synthesis Designs
reading_scope: Primary full text inspected; motivation, orchestration/timing-table method, supported dataflow patterns, comparative evaluation, limitations, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Existing fast HLS simulators do not cover complex dataflow, multithreading, and FIFO interactions well enough.
general_principle: Orchestrate software execution with hardware timing tables and explicit communication semantics.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Empirical agreement with RTL/HLS co-simulation and comparative performance against prior simulators.
practical_connection: Complex HLS dataflow designs and practical design-space iteration.
evaluation_breadth: Eleven reported complex designs with comparative timing and speed results.
artifact_strength: Broad timing/functional simulator evidence; no producer-independent cut/minimality certificate.
narrative_sequence: Coverage gap -> unified simulation architecture -> implementation -> accuracy/speed comparison -> remaining unsupported behavior.
delta_for_this_project: Broadens workload and simulator coverage; the present contribution is a bounded semantic certificate and negative cost boundary.

title: FireSim: FPGA-Accelerated Cycle-Exact Scale-Out System Simulation in the Public Cloud
reading_scope: Archived primary full report inspected; system architecture, decoupled simulation method, deployment, scale-out case studies, performance, and limitations calibrated.
motivating_problem: Cycle-exact simulation of large scale-out systems is too slow and costly in conventional software environments.
general_principle: Map RTL-derived target models and networks onto elastic cloud FPGAs using decoupled host/target interfaces.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Cycle-exact execution is preserved by the FPGA simulation architecture; evidence is large-scale empirical deployment and rate measurements.
practical_connection: Warehouse-scale hardware/software co-design and microarchitectural exploration.
evaluation_breadth: Up to 1,024 nodes / 4,096 cores plus several system-research case studies.
artifact_strength: Open, scalable simulation platform and extensive system evidence; no proof-carrying slice object.
narrative_sequence: Scale-out simulation barrier -> FPGA/cloud architecture -> deployment automation -> large-scale demonstrations -> research uses.
delta_for_this_project: Establishes simulation scale rather than consumer-checkable dependency evidence; this paper deliberately does not compete on speed.

title: Yosys: A Free Verilog Synthesis Suite
reading_scope: Primary full paper inspected visually and textually; motivation, RTLIL architecture, pass framework, use cases, evaluation, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Research needs an open, extensible Verilog synthesis framework rather than opaque commercial flows.
general_principle: Lower HDL into RTLIL and apply modular synthesis/analysis passes before backend emission.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Engineering validation through real designs, pass composition, and comparison/use cases rather than a formal frontend theorem.
practical_connection: The present artifact pins ten unmodified Yosys sources and preserves the upstream ISC notice.
evaluation_breadth: Multiple fine- and coarse-grain synthesis use cases and real-world Verilog support.
artifact_strength: Mature open infrastructure; its parser/lowering remains trusted unless separately validated.
narrative_sequence: Closed-tool barrier -> open RTLIL/pass architecture -> representative flows -> evaluation -> extensibility.
delta_for_this_project: Supplies public inputs and frontend context; the artifact adds accepted-instance source/harness/IR validation plus a separate certificate checker.

title: Reusability is FIRRTL Ground: Hardware Construction Languages, Compiler Frameworks, and Transformations
reading_scope: Primary paper inspected through the IEEE record/full-text route; compiler-IR motivation, FIRRTL design, transformation examples, evaluation, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Hardware construction languages lack a reusable, technology-independent compiler framework comparable to software ecosystems.
general_principle: Use an open typed hardware IR and reusable compiler passes to separate construction languages from technology-specific RTL.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Transformation semantics and engineering case studies demonstrate reuse; the paper does not attach a per-output semantic certificate.
practical_connection: Compiler analyses, optimizations, instrumentations, and specializations for hardware generators.
evaluation_breadth: A broad catalogue of compiler transformations and HCL examples.
artifact_strength: Open IR/compiler foundation with practical transformations; not proof-carrying timing slicing.
narrative_sequence: Hardware reuse gap -> FIRRTL/HCF design -> transformation catalogue -> examples/evaluation -> ecosystem implications.
delta_for_this_project: Clarifies the value of a typed IR; this project fixes a smaller equation semantics and checks observation-specific cut evidence.

title: Kami: A Platform for High-Level Parametric Hardware Specification and Its Modular Verification
reading_scope: Primary full paper inspected; transition-system semantics, modular refinement methodology, Coq automation, multicore case study, evaluation, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Industrial model checking proves isolated properties but does not compose naturally into full-system hardware theorems.
general_principle: Specify Bluespec-style hardware as labeled transition systems in Coq and prove modular refinements compositionally.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Kernel-checked Coq proofs and extraction to synthesizable hardware establish end-to-end functional correctness for the modeled designs.
practical_connection: An infinite family of cache-coherent shared-memory multicore systems with pipelined RISC-V cores.
evaluation_breadth: Parametric multicore and processor components, with proof automation and synthesis path.
artifact_strength: Mechanized specifications and proofs; different object and trust boundary from post-hoc dependency-cut certificates.
narrative_sequence: Compositional proof gap -> Coq hardware semantics -> modular refinement rules -> verified multicore case study -> lessons.
delta_for_this_project: Stronger mechanized design proof, but not a compact consumer-checkable certificate for an untrusted timing-slice producer.

title: ISA Semantics for ARMv8-A, RISC-V, and CHERI-MIPS
reading_scope: Primary full paper inspected through parsed text and available visual pages; language design, executable semantics, theorem-prover generation, validation, architecture case studies, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Large ISA prose specifications are ambiguous, hard to execute, and duplicated across simulators and proof assistants.
general_principle: Define typed executable ISA semantics once in Sail and generate interpreters plus theorem-prover definitions.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Cross-validation against architecture tests, executable models, and proof-assistant backends supports semantic fidelity.
practical_connection: ARMv8-A, RISC-V, and CHERI-MIPS models, including OS-boot and toolchain uses.
evaluation_breadth: Three substantial ISAs and multiple generated backends.
artifact_strength: Shared executable/formal source semantics; not an RTL dependency-slice certificate.
narrative_sequence: ISA-specification duplication -> Sail language and semantics -> generated tools/proofs -> architecture-scale validation -> limitations.
delta_for_this_project: Shows how source semantics can be centralized; this project instead validates a narrow accepted-source lowering and checks bounded timing evidence.

title: Accelerating Precise End-to-End Simulation: Latency-Sensitive Many-Core System Modeling
reading_scope: Primary full text inspected; layered timing model, latency-sensitive components, validation protocol, workloads, performance/accuracy results, and limitations calibrated.
motivating_problem: RTL simulation is too slow while conventional abstractions lose latency interactions important to many-core systems.
general_principle: Compose layered, latency-sensitive component models to retain key end-to-end timing effects.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Empirical comparison against precise reference simulation reports bounded error and substantial speedup.
practical_connection: Large many-core systems and end-to-end workloads.
evaluation_breadth: Reported scaling to 1,024 cores with multiple workloads and component studies.
artifact_strength: Recent broad timing-model evaluation; no replayable semantic certificate for a retained dependency set.
narrative_sequence: Accuracy/speed tension -> layered model -> component integration -> large-scale comparison -> scope.
delta_for_this_project: A close modern timing-model comparator; the present work makes no approximate-performance claim and instead certifies a bounded observation.

title: Rtl2lean: Automated RTL-to-Lean Translation with Hierarchical Theorem Generation and Lemma Reuse
reading_scope: Primary full text inspected; RTL-to-Lean pipeline, theorem hierarchy, lemma reuse, kernel-checking boundary, experiments, threats, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Manual formalization of RTL in theorem provers is labor intensive and impedes scalable proof reuse.
general_principle: Translate RTL automatically into Lean transition models and generate hierarchical theorem libraries with reusable lemmas.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Generated proofs are checked by the Lean kernel; experiments report theorem coverage and lemma reuse across six designs.
practical_connection: Six RTL designs, hundreds of generated theorems, and reusable verification tasks.
evaluation_breadth: Six designs and 403 reported theorems, including reuse and automation measurements.
artifact_strength: Mechanized source/proof chain with a small trusted kernel; translation correctness still depends on the generated encoding and checked theorem statements.
narrative_sequence: Manual-proof bottleneck -> translation/theorem architecture -> proof generation and reuse -> multi-design evaluation -> limitations.
delta_for_this_project: Stronger mechanization of source and proof, whereas this project contributes producer-independent cut, minimality, and canonical-diagnostic certificates for a bounded semantics.

title: Granite: A Modular Methodology for Foundational Verification of Hardware-Software Leakage Contracts
reading_scope: Primary full text inspected; public-observable contract model, Rocq refinement methodology, processor case study, composition, limitations, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Cycle-level timing leakage crosses hardware/software boundaries and is difficult to verify compositionally.
general_principle: Use deterministic public-observable specification machines and modular Rocq refinements for functional and leakage contracts.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Foundational, kernel-checked compositional proofs connect implementation behavior to cycle-level contracts.
practical_connection: A pipelined processor with speculation, interrupts, and I/O.
evaluation_breadth: Substantial processor case study with hardware/software contract composition.
artifact_strength: Mechanized end-to-end confidentiality/refinement evidence; not dependency-slice minimality or first-completion diagnosis.
narrative_sequence: Leakage-contract gap -> public-observable semantics -> modular proof method -> processor proof -> boundaries.
delta_for_this_project: Granite proves stronger end-to-end contracts; the present object is a small bounded certificate accepted independently of the slice producer.

title: Symbolic Model Checking without BDDs
reading_scope: Accessible primary full text inspected; SAT unrolling construction, bounded LTL argument, counterexample handling, experiments, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: BDD-based symbolic model checking can suffer severe memory blow-up.
general_principle: Reduce bounded temporal model checking to propositional satisfiability over finite unrollings.
correctness_or_performance_argument: The bounded encoding connects SAT assignments to finite counterexamples; preliminary experiments compare practical behavior.
practical_connection: Finite-state reactive-system verification and short counterexample generation.
evaluation_breadth: Preliminary benchmark examples from hardware-style model checking.
artifact_strength: Foundational decision procedure, not a delivered observation-specific slice proof.
narrative_sequence: BDD bottleneck -> SAT bounded encoding -> correctness intuition -> implementation/experiments -> bounds.
delta_for_this_project: Supplies the bounded-verification foundation; this project fixes an explicit certificate format and independently replays universal product evidence.

title: SAT-Based Model Checking without Unrolling
reading_scope: Author-hosted primary paper inspected; relative induction, clause propagation, counterexample production, experiments, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Repeated transition unrolling can make SAT-based safety checking inefficient.
general_principle: Incrementally build relatively inductive clauses over approximate reachability frames.
correctness_or_performance_argument: The algorithm converges to an inductive strengthening or returns a counterexample; experiments demonstrate practical generalization.
practical_connection: Safety-property model checking for finite-state transition systems.
evaluation_breadth: Standard model-checking benchmarks and comparison with contemporary SAT approaches.
artifact_strength: Powerful symbolic invariant engine; no proof-carrying dependency-slice bundle in the present sense.
narrative_sequence: Unrolling limitation -> relative induction -> algorithm -> correctness/convergence -> experiments.
delta_for_this_project: Could replace explicit search internally, but the paper's contribution is the consumer-visible evidence contract rather than IC3 itself.

title: Counterexample-Guided Abstraction Refinement
reading_scope: Accessible CMU full text inspected; abstraction construction, spurious-counterexample analysis, refinement, implementation, experiments, and limitations calibrated.
motivating_problem: Manual abstraction is a major obstacle to applying symbolic model checking to industrial designs.
general_principle: Start with a coarse abstraction, analyze spurious counterexamples, and refine only the distinctions needed to eliminate them.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Simulation-based abstraction preserves property reasoning while refinement eliminates spurious traces; NuSMV experiments support effectiveness.
practical_connection: Industrial-style hardware verification, including a reported large Fujitsu IP example.
evaluation_breadth: Several experiments including a design with hundreds of latches and substantial SMV code.
artifact_strength: Foundational abstraction loop; final evidence is not packaged as the bounded cut/minimality certificate defined here.
narrative_sequence: State explosion/manual abstraction -> automatic abstraction -> counterexample analysis/refinement -> implementation -> experiments.
delta_for_this_project: CEGAR discovers a suitable abstraction iteratively; this project checks a supplied final cut and diagnostic order without trusting its search.

title: Translation Validation
reading_scope: Primary institutional full record and paper text inspected; semantic framework, refinement relation, simulation proof method, SIGNAL-to-C case, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Proving every implementation of a complex optimizing translator correct is often impractical.
general_principle: Validate each concrete translation instance in a common semantic framework.
correctness_or_performance_argument: A simulation/refinement proof checks that the produced target implements the submitted source for that run.
practical_connection: Translation from synchronous multi-clock SIGNAL to asynchronous sequential C.
evaluation_breadth: One challenging compiler case used to demonstrate the general validation architecture.
artifact_strength: Directly motivates an untrusted producer plus independent validator; the exact semantics and evidence object differ.
narrative_sequence: Compiler-proof difficulty -> per-instance validation -> common semantics/refinement -> case study -> general requirements.
delta_for_this_project: The source/harness/IR gate follows this principle, while the second checker validates timing preservation, minimality, diagnostics, and output reconstruction.

title: Proof-Carrying Code
reading_scope: Primary full paper inspected; producer/consumer architecture, safety-policy proof representation, checker boundary, examples, costs, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: A host must safely execute code supplied by an untrusted producer without trusting the producer's toolchain.
general_principle: Require the producer to ship a formal safety proof that a small consumer-side checker validates.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Soundness follows from the proof rules and trusted checker/policy; examples demonstrate feasibility and proof-checking costs.
practical_connection: Safe native-code distribution and mobile-code scenarios.
evaluation_breadth: Representative low-level code and proof-construction/checking experiments.
artifact_strength: Canonical proof-carrying architecture; policy and proof object are code-safety rather than timing-slice preservation.
narrative_sequence: Untrusted-code risk -> producer-supplied proof -> consumer checker -> implementation/examples -> trust/cost discussion.
delta_for_this_project: Provides the architectural model; this work instantiates it for bounded first-completion slices with separate source and bundle acceptance gates.

title: Program Slicing
reading_scope: Seminal paper text and authoritative bibliographic record inspected; slicing criterion, construction intuition, examples, uses, and limitations calibrated.
motivating_problem: Debugging and understanding programs is difficult when irrelevant statements obscure a value of interest.
general_principle: Delete statements that cannot affect a selected program point and variable while preserving the criterion's behavior.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Semantic relevance to the slicing criterion defines the retained subset; examples illustrate executable slices.
practical_connection: Debugging, program comprehension, and maintenance.
evaluation_breadth: Illustrative programs rather than a modern large benchmark campaign.
artifact_strength: Foundational semantic idea; no hardware transaction semantics, universal havoc, or proof-carrying certificate.
narrative_sequence: Debugging relevance problem -> slicing criterion -> construction/examples -> applications and limits.
delta_for_this_project: Supplies the root notion of observation-relative deletion; this paper specializes it to bounded synchronous equations and independently checkable evidence.

title: The Program Dependence Graph and Its Use in Optimization
reading_scope: Primary IBM paper/full record inspected; data/control dependence definitions, PDG representation, transformations, incremental update example, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Separate control-flow and data-flow representations complicate optimization and dependence reasoning.
general_principle: Represent essential data and control dependences uniformly in a program dependence graph.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Dependence-preserving graph transformations support optimization; examples include vectorization and incremental updates.
practical_connection: Compiler optimization and transformation infrastructure.
evaluation_breadth: Algorithmic examples and transformation scenarios rather than a broad empirical suite.
artifact_strength: Foundational dependency representation; reachability alone is insufficient for the semantic timing claim here.
narrative_sequence: Representation gap -> PDG definition -> uniform transformations -> incremental optimization -> implications.
delta_for_this_project: Dependency graphs motivate candidates, but preservation and final-context necessity are checked semantically over transaction observations.

title: Efficient Generation of Inductive Validity Cores for Safety Properties
reading_scope: Primary full author manuscript inspected; IVC definition, UNSAT-core algorithm, correctness proof, JKind implementation, evaluation, minimality discussion, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Successful model-checking proofs give little traceability about which model elements were necessary.
general_principle: Extract inductive validity cores using SMT UNSAT support and minimize them under a monotone safety-proof notion.
correctness_or_performance_argument: The algorithm is proved correct and evaluated for speed, diversity, and minimality in JKind/Lustre.
practical_connection: Requirements traceability, overconstraint diagnosis, and coverage analysis.
evaluation_breadth: A benchmark campaign over Lustre safety models with several core-generation variants.
artifact_strength: Closest minimality foundation; its object is a support core for an inductive proof, not a first-completion cut with source/output binding.
narrative_sequence: Proof-traceability gap -> IVC definition -> algorithms and proof -> implementation/evaluation -> diagnostic uses.
delta_for_this_project: The present work explicitly credits monotonicity and greedy inclusion minimality, adding timing-specific positive/negative certificates and canonical witnesses.

title: Algorithms for Computing Minimal Unsatisfiable Subsets of Constraints
reading_scope: Primary full paper inspected through the author/publisher route; MUS/MCS relationship, algorithms, soundness/completeness, variants, experiments, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Users need exact minimal explanations of infeasible constraint systems rather than nonminimal cores.
general_principle: Exploit the dual relationship between minimal correction sets and minimal unsatisfiable subsets to enumerate or extract MUSes.
correctness_or_performance_argument: Soundness/completeness arguments accompany SAT implementations and experimental comparisons.
practical_connection: Diagnosis, explanation, and repair of overconstrained systems.
evaluation_breadth: Boolean SAT benchmarks with several complete and relaxed algorithm variants.
artifact_strength: General exact minimal-conflict machinery; no temporal observation or source-binding semantics.
narrative_sequence: Explanation gap -> MUS/MCS duality -> algorithms -> correctness/variants -> experiments.
delta_for_this_project: Clarifies subset minimality versus minimum cardinality; the certificate here proves necessity in the final retained timing context.

title: QuickXplain: Preferred Explanations and Relaxations for Over-Constrained Problems
reading_scope: Primary full conference paper inspected; preferred-conflict definition, divide-and-conquer algorithm, solver-generic interface, industrial motivation, evaluation/example, and conclusion calibrated.
motivating_problem: Overconstrained systems can have exponentially many conflicts, while users need small preferred explanations and relaxations.
general_principle: Use ordered preferences and divide-and-conquer consistency tests to compute a preferred irreducible conflict.
correctness_or_performance_argument: The recursive procedure preserves conflict/minimality conditions with a solver oracle; examples and industrial use motivate efficiency.
practical_connection: Interactive configuration and other CP/SAT/DL explanation tasks.
evaluation_breadth: Algorithmic examples and industrial configuration context rather than a large uniform benchmark.
artifact_strength: Solver-agnostic minimal-conflict template; no timing semantics or proof-carrying output program.
narrative_sequence: Explanation overload -> preference model -> divide-and-conquer algorithm -> examples/application -> limitations.
delta_for_this_project: Informs ordered deletion/minimality reasoning, while this work additionally certifies shortest lexicographic temporal counterexamples.
